clue.text: Badger changes hands in capital

indicators.note: the left-hand letter is swapped for the right-hand one, L for left becoming R for right

parts.note: to badger someone is to plague them with demands

explanation.surface: A badger in some city swaps paws, or perhaps a nuisance passing to a new owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes hands' turns L (left) into R (right) in PLAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech capital city, a standard example of a capital.

clue.text: Before 10, quietly obtain mixed blocks of colour here

indicators.note: the quiet note and the mixed letters come before the ten in the answer

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: the word obtain is stirred into a new arrangement

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: An instruction to collect jumbled colour cakes before some deadline marked 10.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to the 10-across answer; it is just the Roman numeral X. The mixed letters of obtain make AINTBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A paint set holds little solid blocks of watercolour, so it is where such blocks are found.

clue.text: Cold lecturer left overcoat in hospital department

indicators.note: the reduced coat sits inside the department's letters

parts.note: A&E is accident and emergency, the hospital casualty department

indicators.note: the lecturer has departed, so that letter goes from the coat

parts.note: an ulster is a long loose overcoat

explanation.surface: A chilly academic leaves a coat behind in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads like a direction or a past tense of leaving the coat; it is the lecturer departing from the overcoat word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold in manner, stern and unfriendly, is a synonym.

clue.text: Edict from the Kremlin: "Employ Ford parts"

indicators.note: the car model splits the word for employ

parts.note: to employ something is to use it
the Ka is a small Ford car

explanation.surface: A Russian decree ordering the use of Ford spare parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like car spares; it is a verb saying KA separates USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a decree issued by the Tsar or Russian government, so a Kremlin edict.

clue.text: Did judge, gutted, get told?

indicators.note: a letter from the inside of the word is removed, as innards are taken out

parts.note: to judge a value is to appraise it, so did judge is the past tense

explanation.surface: A question about whether a disappointed judge was given the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like dismay; it takes the inner A out of APPRAISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being informed of something is being told about it.

clue.text: Saw supporter holding one, so tradition has it

indicators.note: the two pieces together keep the numeral between them

parts.note: a saw is an old saying
an ally supports you
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sawn prop holding something up, according to custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the noun for a saying, not the tool or the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said as a common saying puts it, i.e. according to folk tradition.

clue.text: Polls are free for a change around North Dakota

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the state's abbreviation
the letters of are and free are altered into a new order

parts.note: ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: Voting in North Dakota is free of charge, for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges the two words into a nine-letter shell split around the state code.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of referendum: public votes on a single question are polls.

clue.text: Hailstorm in Belgravia area heard in parts of Africa

indicators.note: the stormy letters go inside the postcode

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode district covering Belgravia, written with I for 1
a storm of the word hail, its letters whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Hail pelting smart Belgravia in London, with the noise carrying to Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Belgravia is a wealthy district of central London. 'Hailstorm' is a one-word composite: the storm whirls the letters of hail before they go in.
explanation.definitionFit: This Bantu language is spoken widely across East Africa.

clue.text: Like small eyes, say, in the form of ellipses

definitions.meaning: lower-case letter i's carry a point above them; eyes is a play on the letter's name
an ellipsis is a row of three points marking an omission

explanation.surface: Describing beady little eyes set in oval shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower-case i's bear a point, and ellipses are rows of points, so both are marked with points.

clue.text: Place where horse is docked

indicators.note: the tail is cut off, as a horse's tail may be docked

parts.note: a horse lives in a stall

explanation.surface: A horse's home whose tail has been cut, or a stable spot on a quay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' fits the horse's tail and also cuts the last letter. The single-L spelling is the British one.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something in position is to place it.

clue.text: Polish worker crosses over in hair-raising style

indicators.note: the polish and worker straddle the letter for over

parts.note: to buff something is to polish it
O is the cricket scoresheet abbreviation for an over
a worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: A Polish labourer crossing the border with a big hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised as the nationality; it means buff.
explanation.definitionFit: A puffed-out, back-combed hairdo is literally raised high, a pun on hair-raising.

clue.text: They need dates in 51 Harley St to get treatment

parts.note: fifty is L and one is spelt out as ONE

indicators.note: the letters are treated, worked over into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Patients at a Harley Street clinic need appointments to be treated.
explanation.walkthrough: Harley Street is London's private-medicine street. 'dates' looks like appointments; it means romantic outings.
explanation.definitionFit: Single people placing personal adverts want romantic partners to go out with.

clue.text: Article describes cattle margins dropping as a result

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so the article goes around

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: the outer letters fall away

parts.note: Herefords are a breed of beef cattle

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reporting on cattle with thin profit margins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' means draws around, as a compass describes a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequently, hence: a connecting word marking a conclusion.

clue.text: Big flower in her novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A large bloom appearing in a woman's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower in crosswords is often a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A major European river, and rivers are crossword flowers since they flow.

clue.text: Bet on it endlessly and dream, going bust

definitions.text: Bet on it endlessly and dream, going bust

indicators.note: the letters break apart and are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of it is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler bets endlessly, dreams of a jackpot and goes broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts IT to I; BETON + I + AND + DREAM rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit machine is just the thing to pour money into, dream and lose everything.

clue.text: Answers concerning partners when letter turns up

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: a letter is turned upside down, U inverted resembling N

parts.note: spouses are marriage partners

explanation.surface: Replies about couples arrive once a letter shows up in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' sounds like arriving; it means flipped over, so U becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: Replies and reactions are synonyms for answers.

clue.text: She feeds bouncy wee runts

indicators.note: lively bouncing letters fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman feeding lively little runts of a litter.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to breastfeed another's baby.

clue.text: Explain unknown round container that sits on coffee table

parts.note: to gloss a text is to explain it
Y is a mathematical unknown
a gun's magazine holds the rounds of ammunition

explanation.surface: Explain the strange round tin that lives on the coffee table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is a noun: a cartridge, held in a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiny lifestyle periodicals are the typical reading left out on low lounge tables.

clue.text: Groovy artwork, old copper wrapped in cotton

indicators.note: the abbreviations are enclosed by the fabric word

parts.note: lint is cotton fibre or fluff
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A trendy sixties artwork made of an old copper object wrapped in cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' suggests sixties cool; it means full of grooves.
explanation.definitionFit: A print cut into a lino block, literally full of carved grooves.

clue.text: In the shower he gets scrubbed, making progress

indicators.note: scrubbed means cancelled, so the pronoun is deleted

parts.note: being in a rain shower is being in the rain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man washing himself in the shower while getting on with things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' looks like the bathroom; it is a fall of rain. 'scrubbed' means cancelled, not washed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means under way, in progress, so something going forward.

clue.text: Old tax firm's revolutionary book

indicators.note: turning the whole string backwards, as in a revolution

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
Co. is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An old tax firm's radical book.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read OVATCO, and 'revolutionary' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A book size made from sheets folded into eight leaves.

clue.text: US block or unfinished one elsewhere?

indicators.note: the long word is cut short

parts.note: outside America the full word for this block of flats is used

explanation.surface: An American apartment block, or a half-built one abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The short form is American; elsewhere the full word condominium is used, here truncated.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call an apartment building of owner-occupied units this.

clue.text: Brief answer to clue in eastern river flowing west

indicators.note: the crossword term sits inside the river's letters
in an across entry, west is leftwards, so the river runs backwards

parts.note: the Nene flows through the east of England into the Wash
in crossword jargon a light is a grid answer

explanation.surface: A short answer to a clue about a river in the east running westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective; it is the verb to inform. NENE reads ENEN backwards and takes LIGHT in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to inform them, giving them knowledge.

clue.text: Nasty material's begun getting seized

indicators.note: the letters are gripped inside the two words

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant has started to get stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for sticky, unpleasant muck or goo.

clue.text: Some possess crest, possibly revealing this?

definitions.text: Some possess crest, possibly revealing this?

indicators.note: the word for some holds the other letters

parts.note: any can mean some, as in have you any

indicators.note: the letters of crest are possibly in another order

explanation.surface: Some families own a heraldic crest that reveals their lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as definition: a coat of arms can reveal where a family comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A family crest displays lineage, the line of forebears.

clue.text: Not just dodgems etc don't start

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: bumper cars and similar rides are found at a fairground

explanation.surface: Not merely bumper cars and the like: they won't start up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' means fair, not merely. Dodgems are bumper cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking justice or fairness, so inequitable.

clue.text: Coaches keep time in books? Nothing's more witless

indicators.note: the buses go inside the books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: the buses hold the time letter

parts.note: coaches are buses

explanation.surface: Coaches who keep track of time in their record books are the dimmest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaches' looks like trainers; it means buses.
explanation.definitionFit: If nothing is more stupid, it is the most stupid: a superlative of slow-witted.

clue.text: Notice a knock occasionally interrupting this?

definitions.text: Notice a knock occasionally interrupting this?

indicators.note: the picked letters break into the word for notice

parts.note: to notice is to see

indicators.note: every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Listen for a spirit's rap breaking into a spiritualist session.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as definition: spirits at such sittings are said to answer with knocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering trying to contact spirits, who traditionally answer with knocks.
